name: Business Research Methods
description: Develops skills for conducting rigorous business and social science research — research design, quantitative and qualitative methods, data analysis, literature review, and professional research reporting.

modules.title: Introduction to Research
modules.objectives: Distinguish types of research (basic, applied, exploratory); explain the general research process; compare business and academic research; identify key ethical principles.
modules.readingNote: Open textbook chapter on empirical questions, systematic evidence, and public research claims.
modules.videoNote: No module-specific primary video assigned; use the reading, practice, and self-contained assignment.
modules.practiceNote: Open textbook ethics chapter: identify consent, risk, privacy, and review requirements.
modules.assignment: Submit: the classification table, flowchart, ethics note, and citations. Include: For a fictional neighborhood grocery whose online orders have a high cancellation rate, classify three possible investigations as basic, applied, or exploratory research. Build a six-step research-process flowchart and identify what evidence would be needed before claiming a cause. Add a 150–200 word ethics note covering privacy, consent, and data minimization; do not collect data from real people. Evaluation: correct research-type distinctions, logical process, and appropriate human-subject boundary.

modules.title: Formulating Research Questions
modules.objectives: Identify a research problem from a business context; write clear research objectives and hypotheses; define the scope and limitations of a study.
modules.readingNote: Open textbook guide to empirical, feasible research questions.
modules.videoNote: No module-specific primary video assigned; use the reading, practice, and self-contained assignment.
modules.practiceNote: Open textbook explanation of null hypotheses and evidence-limited testing.
modules.assignment: Submit: a one-page research-question brief. Include: Using the fictional grocery cancellation problem, use the stated fictional evidence to write one measurable research question, define its predictor and outcome, and write a null and alternative hypothesis without promising causation. State the target population, time window, two exclusions, and two limitations. Finish with one sentence explaining what result would not prove. Evaluation: measurable variables, aligned hypotheses, bounded scope, and cautious inference.

modules.title: Literature Review
modules.objectives: Search academic databases effectively; evaluate source credibility; synthesize findings across multiple sources; manage citations using standard formats. Students will interpret sources or examples, explain cause-and-effect relationships, and support claims with evidence in the module assignment.
modules.readingNote: Purdue OWL guidance on synthesizing rather than listing sources.
modules.videoNote: No module-specific primary video assigned; use the reading, practice, and self-contained assignment.
modules.assignment: Submit: the table, synthesis, and references. Include: Use a teacher-provided packet of three accessible articles about online-cart abandonment. Create a source table with author/date, design, sample, main finding, and limitation; then write a 300–400 word synthesis that identifies one convergence, one disagreement, and one unresolved question. Do not claim that reading an abstract equals reviewing a full study. Evaluation: accurate source representation, cross-source synthesis, limitation awareness, and complete citations.

modules.title: Research Design
modules.objectives: Compare exploratory, descriptive, and causal research designs; explain internal and external validity; distinguish reliability from validity in measurement.
modules.readingNote: Open textbook overview of experimental and nonexperimental research designs.
modules.videoNote: No module-specific primary video assigned; use the reading, practice, and self-contained assignment.
modules.practiceNote: Open textbook guide to alternative explanations and internal validity.
modules.assignment: Submit: the three-plan table and recommendation. Include: For a fictional retailer comparing two checkout-page designs, create three plans—exploratory interview analysis, descriptive usage analysis, and a randomized A/B test—without recruiting or contacting anyone. For each, specify data, comparison, validity threat, and claim allowed. Recommend one plan and explain reliability versus validity in 250–300 words. Evaluation: correct design distinctions, realistic threats, and claims matched to design.

modules.title: Quantitative Methods: Surveys
modules.objectives: Design clear and unbiased survey questions; apply Likert scales correctly; choose an appropriate sampling method; plan survey administration and response rate improvement.
modules.readingNote: Open textbook guidance on wording, ordering, response options, and context effects.
modules.videoNote: No module-specific primary video assigned; use the reading, practice, and self-contained assignment.
modules.practiceNote: Open textbook sampling, nonresponse, and survey-administration guidance.
modules.assignment: Submit: the questionnaire and 200-word design memo; collect no personal data. Include: Draft—not administer—an eight-item survey about a fictional delivery app: three balanced Likert items using one consistent scale, two behavior-frequency items with defined time windows, two categorical items, and one optional open response. Annotate one leading or double-barreled draft and show its revision. Add a sampling plan and two nonresponse-bias safeguards. Evaluation: neutral wording, complete scales, aligned sample, and privacy-safe design.

modules.title: Quantitative Methods: Data Collection & Analysis
modules.titleZh: 定量方法：数据收集与分析
modules.objectives: Organize and clean collected data in a spreadsheet; calculate descriptive statistics (mean, median, mode, range, standard deviation); interpret basic inferential results (t-test, correlation).
modules.readingNote: Open textbook methods for mean, median, range, standard deviation, distributions, and outliers.
modules.videoNote: No module-specific primary video assigned; use the reading, practice, and self-contained assignment.
modules.practiceNote: Open textbook checklist for cleaning, documenting, and interpreting data.
modules.assignment: Submit: formulas, outputs, data-cleaning note, and interpretation. Include: Use the fictional weekly order totals {42, 45, 45, 47, 50, 51, 52, 54, 55, 59, 62, 88}. In a spreadsheet, calculate mean, median, mode, range, and sample standard deviation; flag 88 for review without silently deleting it. Compare results with and without 88, document the rule used, and write a 200-word interpretation that does not treat description as causation. Evaluation: reproducible calculations, transparent outlier handling, and evidence-limited conclusion.

modules.title: Qualitative Methods
modules.objectives: Explain when qualitative methods are appropriate; compare interviews, focus groups, observation, and case studies; describe coding and thematic analysis of qualitative data.
modules.readingNote: Open textbook overview of qualitative interviews, observation, coding, and thematic analysis.
modules.videoNote: No module-specific primary video assigned; use the reading, practice, and self-contained assignment.
modules.practiceNote: Open textbook guide to observation, coding, validity, and researcher influence.
modules.assignment: Submit: the codebook, coded excerpts, theme map, and memo. Include: Code a teacher-provided fictional transcript containing six customer comments about grocery pickup. Create an initial codebook with code name, definition, inclusion rule, exclusion rule, and example; code every excerpt and group codes into two or three themes. Write a 200-word memo on ambiguity and researcher influence. Do not interview or identify a real person. Evaluation: traceable codes, themes supported by excerpts, and reflexive limitations.

modules.title: Mixed Methods Research
modules.objectives: Explain rationale for combining quantitative and qualitative approaches; describe sequential, concurrent, and transformative mixed-methods designs; define triangulation and its role in improving credibility.
modules.readingNote: Open textbook comparison of qualitative and quantitative approaches, including triangulation.
modules.videoNote: No module-specific primary video assigned; use the reading, practice, and self-contained assignment.
modules.practiceNote: Open textbook guide to quantitative relationships and cautious interpretation.
modules.assignment: Submit: the design diagram, joint display, and 250-word rationale. Include: Design a hypothetical sequential mixed-methods study of a fictional retailer’s cancellation problem. Specify a quantitative data source, a follow-up qualitative source using fictional or teacher-provided data, the integration point, and a joint-display table showing how convergent, complementary, or conflicting results would be handled. Do not recruit participants or collect live data. Evaluation: purposeful method sequence, explicit integration, and honest treatment of disagreement.

modules.title: Data Visualization
modules.objectives: Select the correct chart type for a given data set; apply principles of good visualization (clarity, accuracy, avoid chartjunk); create a basic dashboard summarizing research findings.
modules.readingNote: Open textbook guidance for clear, self-contained tables and graphs that do not repeat or distort results.
modules.videoNote: No module-specific primary video assigned; use the reading, practice, and self-contained assignment.
modules.practiceNote: Open textbook guide to distributions and descriptive summaries.
modules.assignment: Submit: the three valid charts, the before/after correction, data table, and 200-word selection rationale. Include: Use fictional monthly orders Jan–Jun = 120, 135, 128, 150, 162, 171 and channel shares web=55%, app=30%, phone=15%. Create a line chart for time, a bar chart for channel shares, and one intentionally misleading chart that truncates the y-axis. Correct the misleading chart and annotate what changed. Evaluation: chart-task fit, accurate scales/labels, reproducible data, and distortion analysis.

modules.title: Market Research
modules.objectives: Define market research and its role in business decisions; conduct a basic SWOT and PESTLE analysis; analyze consumer behavior patterns; evaluate competitors using secondary data.
modules.readingNote: OpenStax Principles of Marketing §6.1: marketing information and the research process.
modules.videoNote: No module-specific primary video assigned; use the reading, practice, and self-contained assignment.
modules.practiceNote: OpenStax strategic-planning section: situational analysis and external context.
modules.assignment: Submit: both matrices, evidence trail, and recommendation. Include: Use a teacher-provided dossier for a fictional refillable-bottle company. Build a SWOT matrix with evidence tags and a PESTLE table that separates internal from external factors. Choose one strategic question, cite three dossier facts, and write a 250-word recommendation with one counterargument and one missing-data caveat. Do not research or contact a real company. Evaluation: correct factor placement, cited evidence, and caveated strategy.

modules.title: Financial Research & Analysis
modules.objectives: Read and interpret income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements; calculate and interpret key financial ratios; benchmark a company's performance against industry peers.
modules.readingNote: U.S. SEC investor guide to the structure and interpretation of Form 10-K; classroom use only.
modules.videoNote: No module-specific primary video assigned; use the reading, practice, and self-contained assignment.
modules.practiceNote: OpenStax Principles of Finance §5.2: balance-sheet structure and accounting relationships.
modules.assignment: Submit: calculations, a comparison table, and analysis. Include: For fictional Northstar Retail, use current assets $240,000; current liabilities $120,000; total debt $300,000; equity $200,000; revenue $800,000; net income $64,000. Calculate current ratio, debt-to-equity, net profit margin, and return on equity; show formulas and units. Write a 250-word evidence-based analysis with one limitation per ratio and no investment recommendation. Evaluation: correct formulas/results, appropriate denominator, and non-advisory interpretation.

modules.title: Writing the Research Report
modules.objectives: Structure a business research report (introduction, methodology, findings, discussion, conclusion); apply academic writing style; write objectively, clearly, and concisely; integrate evidence from sources.
modules.readingNote: Open textbook structure for transparent empirical reports.
modules.videoNote: No module-specific primary video assigned; use the reading, practice, and self-contained assignment.
modules.practiceNote: Purdue OWL guide to organizing evidence and qualified claims.
modules.assignment: Submit: the report and a checklist mapping each claim to evidence. Include: Using the fictional data and methods from Modules 6 or 9, draft a 600–800 word mini-report with research question, method, results, discussion, limitations, and conclusion. Include a reproducible data table or figure, separate observed results from interpretation, and cite the assigned sources. Do not fabricate participants or claim statistical significance that was not tested. Evaluation: complete structure, reproducibility, result/interpretation separation, and qualified conclusion.

modules.title: Presenting Research
modules.objectives: Write a professional executive summary; design a clear and compelling slide deck; apply data storytelling principles to communicate findings; handle audience questions confidently.
modules.readingNote: Open textbook guidance for concise research talks, slides, and audience questions.
modules.videoNote: No module-specific primary video assigned; use the reading, practice, and self-contained assignment.
modules.practiceNote: Open textbook standards for readable, self-contained figures and tables.
modules.assignment: Submit: slides, notes, summary, and citations. Include: Create a six-slide briefing from the fictional mini-report: title/question, method, two results slides, limitation, and recommendation. Each results slide must cite its data and use a readable chart or table; speaker notes must state what the evidence does and does not support. Add a 150-word executive summary and three anticipated questions with evidence-based answers. Evaluation: narrative coherence, legible evidence, claim discipline, and prepared responses.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes applied research?
options: Research conducted purely to expand knowledge with no immediate use
Research aimed at solving a specific practical problem
Research that uses only qualitative methods
questions.answer: Research aimed at solving a specific practical problem
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Research aimed at solving a specific practical problem.

questions.question: Which is the correct sequence of the research process?
options: Collect data → Define problem → Analyze → Report
Define problem → Literature review → Design → Collect → Analyze → Report
questions.answer: Define problem → Literature review → Design → Collect → Analyze → Report
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Define problem → Literature review → Design → Collect → Analyze → Report.

questions.question: A research hypothesis is best described as:
options: A proven fact supported by all studies
A testable prediction about the relationship between variables
A research question reworded as a statement
questions.answer: A testable prediction about the relationship between variables
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: A testable prediction about the relationship between variables.

questions.question: In this course, which Boolean operator narrows a Google Scholar search by requiring both terms to appear?
questions.answer: AND
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: AND. Students need to recognize why AND matches the evidence in the question and why nearby options do not.

questions.question: Internal validity in an experiment refers to:
options: The extent to which observed differences can be attributed to the independent variable rather than confounds
How well results apply to other settings and populations
The extent to which a sample represents its target population
The consistency of a measure across repeated administrations
questions.answer: The extent to which observed differences can be attributed to the independent variable rather than confounds
questions.explanation: Strong internal validity supports a causal interpretation within the study by ruling out plausible alternative explanations such as confounding variables; it is distinct from generalizability and reliability.

questions.question: A Likert scale question typically asks respondents to:
options: Choose one answer from a yes/no option
Rank items from most to least important
Rate their level of agreement on a scale (e.g., 1–5)
questions.answer: Rate their level of agreement on a scale (e.g., 1–5)
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Rate their level of agreement on a scale (e.g., 1–5).

questions.question: Random sampling is preferable to convenience sampling because it:
options: Ensures every member of the population has an equal chance of being selected
questions.answer: Ensures every member of the population has an equal chance of being selected
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Ensures every member of the population has an equal chance of being selected.

questions.question: Which option best completes this statement? The mean of the data set {4, 8, 6, 10, 2} is:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: 6. The choice fits the prompt because it applies the central rule or concept from Business Research Methods midterm concepts.

questions.question: Standard deviation measures:
options: The middle value in a dataset
The average distance of data points from the mean
The difference between the maximum and minimum values
questions.answer: The average distance of data points from the mean
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: The average distance of data points from the mean. This reinforces the Business Research Methods midterm concepts idea behind the item instead of rewarding a surface-level guess.

questions.question: Which qualitative method involves observing participants in their natural environment without intervening?
questions.answer: Ethnographic observation
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Ethnographic observation. It connects the correct answer to Business Research Methods midterm concepts and separates it from plausible distractors.

questions.question: Focus groups are most useful for:
options: Generating rich qualitative insights through group discussion
questions.answer: Generating rich qualitative insights through group discussion
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Generating rich qualitative insights through group discussion.

questions.question: Which option best completes this statement? Thematic analysis in qualitative research involves:
options: Identifying recurring patterns or themes across qualitative data
Removing all context from interview data
questions.answer: Identifying recurring patterns or themes across qualitative data
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Identifying recurring patterns or themes across qualitative data.

questions.question: Explain the difference between a research question and a hypothesis. Give one example of each for a business research topic.
questions.answer: A research question asks what the study seeks to learn; a hypothesis predicts an expected relationship. Example: RQ: How does response time affect customer retention? Hypothesis: Faster response time increases repeat purchase rate.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: .

questions.question: Describe two advantages and one disadvantage of using surveys as a data collection method in business research.
questions.answer: Surveys can reach many respondents efficiently and produce comparable quantitative data, but they may suffer from low response quality or self-report bias.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: .

questions.question: What is source credibility and why does it matter in a literature review? Name two criteria for evaluating whether a source is credible.
questions.answer: Source credibility means a source is trustworthy, relevant, current, and authoritative. It matters because weak sources lead to weak conclusions; evaluate author expertise, publication venue, evidence quality, date, and bias.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: .

questions.question: In this course, which research design is most appropriate when a researcher wants to establish cause and effect?
questions.answer: Experimental design
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Experimental design. Students need to recognize why Experimental design matches the evidence in the question and why nearby options do not.

questions.question: Triangulation in mixed methods research means:
options: Cross-verifying findings using multiple data sources or methods
Drawing a triangle diagram of results
questions.answer: Cross-verifying findings using multiple data sources or methods
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Cross-verifying findings using multiple data sources or methods.

questions.question: Which chart type is best for showing change over time?
questions.answer: Line chart
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Line chart. It connects the correct answer to Business Research Methods final concepts and separates it from plausible distractors.

questions.question: PESTLE analysis examines which set of external factors?
options: People, Economics, Strategy, Trade, Law, Environment
Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal, Environmental
Product, Entry, Sales, Trade, Location, Equity
Price, Earnings, Stock, Technology, Labor, Exports
questions.answer: Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal, Environmental
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal, Environmental.

questions.question: Which option best completes this statement? A SWOT analysis is used to:
options: Map a company's internal strengths and weaknesses alongside external opportunities and threats
Calculate the mean of survey responses
Test whether two variables are statistically independent
Replace a literature review with financial data
questions.answer: Map a company's internal strengths and weaknesses alongside external opportunities and threats
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Map a company's internal strengths and weaknesses alongside external opportunities and threats.

questions.question: In Business Research Methods final concepts, The current ratio measures:

A company's ability to pay short-term obligations using current assets
Total debt relative to total equity
Return on investment over one year
questions.answer: A company's ability to pay short-term obligations using current assets
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: A company's ability to pay short-term obligations using current assets.

questions.question: Which financial statement shows revenues and expenses over a period?
questions.answer: Income statement
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Income statement. It ties the answer to the historical, civic, geographic, or economic concept being assessed.

questions.question: In a research report, the methodology section should explain:

How data was collected, from whom, and how it was analyzed
A summary of all prior studies
The financial cost of the research
questions.answer: How data was collected, from whom, and how it was analyzed
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: How data was collected, from whom, and how it was analyzed.

questions.question: Which option best completes this statement? An executive summary should:
options: Summarize the main purpose, findings, and recommendations concisely
Contain every detail from the full report
List only raw data tables without interpretation
questions.answer: Summarize the main purpose, findings, and recommendations concisely
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Summarize the main purpose, findings, and recommendations concisely.

questions.question: Data storytelling in a presentation means:

Using fictional examples to explain statistics
Framing data insights within a compelling narrative to guide the audience's understanding
Avoiding charts in favor of written text
questions.answer: Framing data insights within a compelling narrative to guide the audience's understanding
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Framing data insights within a compelling narrative to guide the audience's understanding.

questions.question: Which sampling method divides the population into subgroups and samples from each proportionally?
questions.answer: Stratified sampling
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Stratified sampling. The choice fits the prompt because it applies the central rule or concept from Business Research Methods final concepts.

questions.question: External validity refers to:
options: Whether the study measures what it intends to measure
The degree to which research findings can be generalized to other contexts or populations
questions.answer: The degree to which research findings can be generalized to other contexts or populations
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: The degree to which research findings can be generalized to other contexts or populations.

questions.question: In this course, which of the following is an example of primary data collection?
questions.answer: Conducting original interviews with consumers
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Conducting original interviews with consumers. It connects the correct answer to Business Research Methods final concepts and separates it from plausible distractors.

questions.question: Response bias in surveys occurs when:

The researcher uses too many Likert questions
Data is analyzed using the wrong statistical test
questions.answer: Respondents answer questions inaccurately due to social desirability or misunderstanding
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Respondents answer questions inaccurately due to social desirability or misunderstanding.

questions.question: Debt-to-equity ratio is calculated as:
options: Net income divided by total revenue
Total liabilities divided by shareholders' equity
Current assets divided by current liabilities
Operating income divided by interest expense
questions.answer: Total liabilities divided by shareholders' equity
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Total liabilities divided by shareholders' equity. It connects the correct answer to Business Research Methods final concepts and separates it from plausible distractors.

questions.question: Qualitative research is especially valuable when:
options: Precise numerical measurement is the goal
The researcher seeks to understand meanings, experiences, or social processes in depth
Variables can be easily controlled in a lab
questions.answer: The researcher seeks to understand meanings, experiences, or social processes in depth
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: The researcher seeks to understand meanings, experiences, or social processes in depth.

questions.question: In this course, which principle of good data visualization states that chart elements should not distort the data's true proportions?
questions.answer: Graphical integrity
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Graphical integrity. It connects the correct answer to Business Research Methods final concepts and separates it from plausible distractors.

questions.question: Describe the structure of a complete business research report and explain the purpose of each major section.
questions.answer: A complete business research report usually includes executive summary, research question, background/literature review, method, findings, analysis, recommendations, limitations, and references.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: .

questions.question: Compare and contrast quantitative and qualitative research methods. Give one situation where each would be more appropriate for a business problem.
questions.answer: Quantitative methods measure patterns with numbers and are useful for surveys or experiments; qualitative methods explore meaning and context through interviews or observation. Use quantitative work for market-size estimates and qualitative work to understand customer motivation.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: .

questions.question: Explain the role of market research in business decision-making. How can SWOT and PESTLE analyses complement each other?
questions.answer: Market research reduces uncertainty in decisions. SWOT summarizes internal strengths/weaknesses and external opportunities/threats, while PESTLE scans political, economic, social, technological, legal, and environmental forces.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: .

quizQuestions.explanation: The correct answer is: Basic (pure) research. It connects the correct answer to Introduction to Research and separates it from plausible distractors.

quizQuestions.question: Business research differs from purely academic research in that it primarily aims to:

quizQuestions.answer: Solve specific organizational problems or support decisions

quizQuestions.question: Which feature most clearly distinguishes exploratory research from a confirmatory test?
options: It begins with a fixed causal estimate
It is used to clarify a poorly defined problem and generate possibilities
It always uses a nationally representative sample
It requires a statistically significant result

Specific, focused, and answerable through research

The research question in question form

quizQuestions.explanation: The correct answer is: That there is no significant relationship or difference between variables.

quizQuestions.explanation: The correct answer is: The boundaries that define what the research will and will not cover.

Which device did you use for your last order?

To prove the survey is unbiased

quizQuestions.explanation: The correct answer is: Mean. The explanation asks students to connect the answer with cause, evidence, or consequence rather than memorizing a term.

Summarize and describe the features of a dataset
quizQuestions.answer: Summarize and describe the features of a dataset

quizQuestions.question: For the ordered data {3, 7, 7, 9, 12}, which statement is correct?
options: The median is 7 and the mode is 7
The median is 9 and there is no mode
The mean is 7 and the range is 7
The median is 7 and the range is 7
quizQuestions.answer: The median is 7 and the mode is 7
quizQuestions.explanation: With five ordered values, the third value gives a median of 7, and 7 is also the only repeated value, so it is the mode; the range is 12−3=9.
